transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-27 15:00 PST
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Lena Park (CTO, CodeBridge), Samir Patel (Platform), Jocelyn Rivera (Backend)

Auto-summary (auto): Live walkthrough of SDK integration, focusing on auth patterns for local dev and CI, environment variables, secrets management, and quickstart snippets in Python and TypeScript. Security questions around VPC/private deployment, encryption and audit logs.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Avery: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro, I'm Avery with Redwood, AE on the account, and Marco is our solution engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:18] Lena: Good, thanks. Excited to see the SDK flow. We want to get devs unblocked this week.
[00:26] Marco: Awesome, today's plan — a short console tour, then live code: Python then TS, auth patterns, CI and secrets, and finish with next steps and a perf pilot scope.
[00:40] Samir: Sounds good, our main constraints — sub-150ms latency for customer-facing routes and strict pedigree on keys, we run everything in AWS EKS and use HashiVault for secrets.
[00:54] Avery: Great, that's helpful context. Quick question — do you expect to go hosted first or are you looking at private right away?
[01:02] Lena: We prefer hosted for fast dev but will need private (VPC) for production because of compliance for some clients. Also KMS is required for certain data.
[01:14] Marco: Understood. Redwood supports that workflow: start hosted for dev and staging, then Dedicated or Private for prod. Private gives you the customer-managed VPC and K M S integration. We'll send the exact network diagram.
[01:33] Jocelyn: How about data retention and logs? We need audit logs and the ability to purge chat content.
[01:40] Avery: We have audit logs and retention controls. We'll include the SOC2/ISO bits in the security pack.
[01:48] Marco: Ok, jumping into the console — I'm sharing my screen, top-left is the model catalog, right now you can see latency profiles and throughput for each model. For quickstarts, the console gives you one-click token creation.
[02:10] [screen share pause] Marco: For SDK examples, start by setting environment vars. For local dev we recommend REDWOOD_API_KEY in a .env loaded by dotenv. For CI, store the key in your vault and inject into the build environment as REDWOOD_API_KEY.
[02:33] Samir: Do you have an example for GitHub Actions?
[02:36] Marco: Yes, small snippet: name: CI-step run: export REDWOOD_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.REDWOOD_API_KEY }} then run the test script. We'll attach the full example in the repo.
[02:50] [slight crosstalk]
[03:05] Marco: Now Python quickstart — show code: from redwood import RedwoodClient client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ.get('REDWOOD_API_KEY')) response = client.generate("Hello world")
[03:32] Jocelyn: The package name — is it redwood or redwood-client?
[03:36] Marco: It's currently "redwood" in PyPI, but sometimes the package naming in docs lags. We'll confirm the exact pip name and add it to the repo readme.
[03:49] Marco: For streaming, we demonstrate using the stream() iterator; remember streaming needs websockets or HTTP/2 depending on environment. We'll include examples.
[04:12] [00:04:12] Avery: On TypeScript, import { RedwoodClient } from '@redwoodai/sdk' // example then new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY })
[04:28] Samir: We run serverless Lambdas for some routes; any gotchas for cold starts with the SDK?
[04:35] Marco: Good question — we provide lightweight client initialization and recommend reusing clients across invocations when possible. For cold-start sensitive paths, consider pinned smaller models or Dedicated capacity to reduce variance.
[04:56] [04:56] Jocelyn: How does KV cache behave? We saw notes about prefix caching.
[05:03] Marco: The KV cache — sometimes transcribed as K V cash in docs — is automatic for repeated prefixes if you enable caching; our SDK exposes a cache config to control TTL and scope (global vs per-tenant). We'll show a sample in the repo.
[05:30] Lena: Can we rotate keys? We rotate nightly.
[05:33] Avery: Yes, you can rotate keys; best practice is short-lived tokens via your Vault and to use the key rollover endpoints. We'll include a script.
[05:45] Samir: For private deployments, how do you handle egress and firewall rules?
[05:50] Marco: In Private mode, we deploy into your V P C and you control subnets and firewall. Our control plane can be customer-managed. We'll include the network diagram and required ACLs.
[06:10] [06:10] Marco: Quick demo switch — live code: I'm opening the sample repo. First file is python/quickstart.py — shows setting env, instantiate client, send request, handle streaming.
[06:28] Marco: Now TypeScript sample: ts/examples/quickstart.ts uses fetch-based streaming example for Node 18 and shows how to handle tokens.
[06:41] Jocelyn: For the embeddings flow, does your SDK batch automatically?
[06:45] Marco: Yes, we have an embeddings helper that batches by size and by tokens; you can tune batch_size. For large batches we recommend background workers so you don't block request threads.
[07:02] Lena: Can we control quantization or model variant selection via the SDK call?
[07:06] Marco: You can specify model variants and quantization profiles in the request payload or pin the default in the console per-route. Redwood Optimize also makes suggestions for quantization based on workload. Sometimes docs call it Redwood Optimizer in older notes — we'll correct that.
[07:28] [07:28] Samir: Security question — do you support HSM-backed keys?
[07:31] Marco: Yes, customers can bring their own K M S or HSM for encryption at rest. We'll include the KMS integration guide.
[07:44] Jocelyn: On CI secrets, we prefer not to put long-lived keys in GitHub secrets. Any short-lived flow here?
[07:51] Avery: We recommend short-lived tokens minted by an internal service using Redwood's token creation API, then inject into the CI job just-in-time. We'll provide an example service code.
[08:05] [08:05] Marco: Switching back to console: here's the routes page where you can map an endpoint to a model and set rollout policy. For canary you can route 10% to a new version.
[08:24] Lena: That helps for gradual rollout.
[08:29] Marco: Now let's run a quick local demo — I'll run the python quickstart to show a generation and then a streaming example.
[08:45] [08:45] [terminal running noises]
[09:05] Marco: Ok generation returned in ~120ms for this small prompt on hosted model. Note this is a small sample; we'll run your real payloads in the perf POC.
[09:16] Jocelyn: Nice. Can we run the perf runner against Dedicated when we move to prod?
[09:20] Marco: Yes, part of the pilot we can provision a short reserved pool or burst capacity. We'll outline cost impacts in the pricing doc.
[09:34] [09:34] Samir: About monitoring — does the console expose per-token costs per route?
[09:38] Avery: Yes, token-level breakdowns per route and model are available, and you can set quotas. The Console also surfaces regression alerts tied to eval prompt sets.
[09:51] [09:51] Jocelyn: Any gotchas for embedding vector sizes? We use 1536 vectors currently.
[09:55] Marco: That's supported; we have different models and vector sizes. The embeddings API handles most sizes; for storage and nearest-neighbor performance you should tune batch size and sharding.
[10:10] Marco: Quick note — sample env vars in repo: REDWOOD_API_KEY, REDWOOD_REGION optional if you want a region override. For private deployments the endpoint changes to your private control plane URL and you supply a client certificate or managed auth token. We'll provide exact env examples.
[10:32] [10:32] Lena: Will you include a small Dockerfile for running quickstarts in a build container?
[10:36] Marco: Yes, docker/quickstart.Dockerfile is in the repo. It shows how to pass REDWOOD_API_KEY via build-time or runtime secrets.
[10:48] [10:48] Samir: About rate limits — can we request higher per-route throughput?
[10:52] Avery: For Dedicated customers we set SLO and throughput via reserved GPU pools. For hosted there are tiered rates; we'll put the options in the pricing sheet.
[11:04] Marco: Jumping ahead to perf pilot scope — we propose a 2-week pilot: week 1 smoke tests and tuning, week 2 full load runs. Need your sample payloads and 95th and p95 targets.
[11:20] Lena: We can provide payloads and an initial SLO of 150ms p95, throughput 50 rps for the customer-facing path.
[11:28] [11:28] Marco: Noted. We'll create a perf runner that uses your payloads and runs with variable concurrency.
[11:40] Jocelyn: A quick question on rollout SDK: how do we do A/B tests via the SDK?
[11:45] Marco: You can set per-request metadata headers to route in the control plane, or set a rollout policy in console for a route. The SDK exposes per-request route selection.
[11:58] [11:58] [slight pause]
[12:10] Marco: Ok final section — debugging tips: enable verbose trace headers, send us sample request/response IDs and we can pull X-ray traces. For long-running sessions we recommend KV cache with TTL to speed up repeated prompts.
[12:30] Samir: If we run into model quality regressions, do you support eval sets?
[12:34] Avery: Yes, Redwood Optimize lets you tie evals to regression alerts and rollbacks. We'll include an example eval suite and prompt set.
[12:46] Lena: Thanks, this has been very practical.
[12:50] Marco: Wrapping up — recapping next steps. I'll summarize and then Avery will follow up with the security pack and repo link.
[13:02] Avery: Action items: I'll send SOC2 docs and repo, Marco will share perf script, and we'll schedule the POC. Any blockers?
[13:12] Jocelyn: None from our side. We want the sandbox access so we can run smoke tests.
[13:18] Avery: We'll do that.
[13:22] [13:22] Lena: One last quickie — pricing estimate for 50 rps and Dedicated baseline?
[13:28] Avery: We'll include back-of-envelope in the follow-up, and the pricing sheet will show Dedicated reserved options.
[13:35] Marco: All right, I'll drop the repo link in chat now and then follow-up email with attachments.
[13:43] [13:43] Avery: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with concrete items.
[13:49] Lena: Thanks!
[13:50] [call ends]

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings (e.g., K V cash for KV cache; Redwood Optimizer vs Redwood Optimize). Some speaker labels may be simplified.
